chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, who said:

I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), and I said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you. In all matters they sought to extinguish your light and to demean you, until they lodged you in this most repulsive inn, the inn of the vagabonds.”

So he said: “Here, O Ibn Saʿīd.” Then he gestured with his hand and said: “Look.” So I looked, and there I was amidst elegant gardens and radiant gardens, in which were excellent fragrant ones, and youths as though they were hidden pearls, and birds, and gazelles, and rivers gushing forth. Then my sight was bewildered and my eye grew weary.
So he said: “Wherever we may be, this is made ready for us; we are not in the inn of the vagabonds.”

key_terms.إِطْفَاءَ نُورِكَ: attempting to extinguish the Imam’s light, meaning to suppress his divine guidance and manifest rank
key_terms.اللُّؤْلُؤُ الْمَكْنُونُ: hidden pearls, describing the purity and beauty of the youths seen in the vision
key_terms.الْخَانَ الْأَشْنَعَ: the most repulsive inn, indicating an outwardly degrading place of lodging
key_terms.بِرَوْضَاتٍ آنِقَاتٍ: amidst elegant gardens, referring to a beautiful unseen garden-like realm
key_terms.خَانَ الصَّعَالِيكِ: the inn of vagabonds or destitute people, used here to describe social humiliation
key_terms.عَتِيدٌ: prepared and made ready, indicating what has been readied for the Imam (عليه السلام)

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the unseen dignity and divine station of Imam Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) despite worldly humiliation?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Imam Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), despite being placed in a degrading lodging by his enemies, disclosed to Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd a hidden realm of splendid gardens and blessings prepared for him. It highlights the exalted rank of the Imam (عليه السلام) and shows that outward humiliation does not diminish the divine honor and unseen station granted to the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).
